title: [Cache] A huge stale-while-revalidate value overflows DateTime in CacheEntry.IsStaleWhileRevalidate and poisons MemoryCacheStorage
body:
## Summary
ParseCacheControl stores stale-while-revalidate unclamped, and CacheEntry.IsStaleWhileRevalidate adds it to ExpiresAtUtc with an unchecked DateTime addition. A peer that sends a value above about 2.5e11 seconds makes that addition throw once the entry is stale, so the URL can no longer be fetched and the storage sweep throws inside every later SetAsync. Any client using CacheInterceptor against an untrusted origin or a MITM on plain http is affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheEntry.cs:161`

## Problem
ParseCacheControl (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:103-112) accepts any stale-while-revalidate that fits TimeSpan (up to ~9.22e11 s) and stores it unclamped. CacheEntry.IsStaleWhileRevalidate (CacheEntry.cs:160-161) computes `ExpiresAtUtc.Value + StaleWhileRevalidate.Value` once the entry is stale and has a validator; for a value above ~2.52e11 s the sum exceeds DateTime.MaxValue and DateTime.op_Addition throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException (ExpiresAtUtc is clamped by AddClamped, this sum is not). Callers: the foreground lookup at CacheInterceptor.cs:352 (throws before the entry can be removed at :378), and CacheEntry.ShouldEvict (CacheEntry.cs:173) used by MemoryCacheStorage.RemoveExpiredEntriesUnsafe (MemoryCacheStorage.cs:274), which SetAsync runs at :92 after it already removed the key being replaced (:89-90) and before `_nextExpiredSweepUtc` is advanced (:285-286). GetCountAsync/GetSizeAsync (:169, :185) hit the same sweep. No test uses a stale-while-revalidate other than 60.

**Failure scenario.** Any origin the client talks to (or a MITM on http) answers one GET with `Cache-Control: max-age=1, stale-while-revalidate=300000000000` and an ETag. After 1 s: (1) every GET of that URL throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the cache interceptor and never reaches the network; (2) the next due sweep throws inside SetAsync and, because the sweep deadline is never advanced, every later SetAsync for any key of any host throws: nothing new is cached (logged as 'Store failed'), and a 304 revalidation of an unrelated entry first loses that entry (removed at :89-90) and then fails the caller's request, because CompleteNotModifiedRevalidationAsync awaits the store (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:60-63). The poisoned entry is never evicted (the LRU loop is after the throwing sweep); only ClearAsync, Dispose or an unsafe-method invalidation of that URL removes it.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 1.2.2; RFC 5861 3

## Suggested fix
Clamp stale-while-revalidate when parsing (RFC 9111 section 1.2.2 style, e.g. to 2^31 s) and compute the window with an overflow-safe add (reuse AddClamped) in IsStaleWhileRevalidate. Make the storage sweep tolerant of a throwing entry (evict it). Add a regression test with a stale entry carrying stale-while-revalidate=300000000000.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] stale-while-revalidate is clamped when parsed (2^31 seconds, RFC 9111 section 1.2.2) and IsStaleWhileRevalidate uses an overflow-safe add
- [ ] A stale entry carrying stale-while-revalidate=300000000000 is served, revalidated or evicted without throwing
- [ ] MemoryCacheStorage sweeps and SetAsync keep working when one stored entry is malformed; the offending entry is evicted
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-protocol-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ParseCacheControl stores stale-while-revalidate unclamped (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:103-112); values between ~2.52e11 s (DateTime.MaxValue minus now) and ~9.22e11 s fit TimeSpan. CacheEntry.IsStaleWhileRevalidate (Runtime/Cache/CacheEntry.cs:160-161) evaluates `ExpiresAtUtc.Value + StaleWhileRevalidate.Value` only once now >= ExpiresAtUtc; DateTime.op_Addition throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. ExpiresAtUtc is clamped (AddClamped, Parsing.cs:200-209), this sum is not. Callers have no guard: foreground lookup CacheInterceptor.cs:352 (EnableRevalidation defaults true, :26) throws before the removal at :378; MemoryCacheStorage.RemoveExpiredEntriesUnsafe (:274) calls ShouldEvict -> IsStaleWhileRevalidate (CacheEntry.cs:173), and MaybeSweepExpiredEntriesUnsafe advances _nextExpiredSweepUtc only after the sweep returns (:285-286), so once the 15 s interval elapses every SetAsync throws at :92, after it already removed the key being replaced (:89-90). StorePreparedEntryAsync swallows it as 'Store failed' (CacheInterceptor.cs:983-986), but the 304 path uses StorePreparedEntryCoreAsync without a catch (:1039-1048) and is awaited in the foreground (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:60-63), so unrelated revalidations lose their entry and fail. GetCountAsync/GetSizeAsync (:169, :185) hit the same sweep. No test uses a stale-while-revalidate other than 60 (rg over Tests/Runtime/Cache). No open issue.

Related: [[R11-cache-protocol-05]].

title: [Cache] Cache-Control parsing lets the last duplicate directive win, falls back to Expires on invalid max-age and splits quoted strings on commas
body:
## Summary
ParseCacheControl splits the header with Split(',') without quoted-string handling, overwrites earlier max-age and stale-while-revalidate occurrences, and ignores an unparsable max-age so freshness falls back to Expires. Responses with conflicting or malformed directives can therefore be served fresh for much longer than RFC 9111 allows. Callers of CacheInterceptor are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:30`

## Problem
ParseCacheControl splits each field line with `value.Split(',')` (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:30) without honouring quoted-string, so the members of `ext="a, max-age=600, b"` are parsed as real directives; `private="..."` does not match the exact-string compare at :59 and is ignored. Each max-age/stale-while-revalidate occurrence overwrites the previous one (:99, :112). A max-age that does not parse is skipped (:93-97), so ResolveExpiry falls back to Expires (:140-159).

**Failure scenario.** `Cache-Control: max-age=0, max-age=3600` is served fresh for an hour (RFC 9111 section 4.2.1: use the first occurrence or consider the response stale). `Cache-Control: max-age=1h` with `Expires` a year ahead is fresh for a year, where the RFC encourages treating invalid freshness information as stale. `Cache-Control: no-cache="set-cookie, max-age=600"` picks up a max-age from inside a quoted argument.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.2.1, 5.2

## Suggested fix
Tokenize with quoted-string awareness, keep the first occurrence of a directive (or mark the response stale on conflicting duplicates), and mark the response stale when max-age is present but invalid instead of consulting Expires.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Cache-Control is tokenized with quoted-string awareness so directives inside a quoted argument are not parsed
- [ ] The first occurrence of a duplicated freshness directive is used, or the response is treated as stale on conflict (RFC 9111 section 4.2.1)
- [ ] A present but invalid max-age makes the response stale instead of consulting Expires
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Large delta-seconds in max-age, s-maxage and stale-while-revalidate throw OverflowException from TimeSpan.FromSeconds instead of clamping
body:
## Summary
ParseCacheControl passes long.TryParse results straight to TimeSpan.FromSeconds, which throws for 12 to 19 digit values, and silently drops 20+ digit values. A 304 revalidation response carrying such a value fails the caller's request with a non-UHttpException, and a 200 with one is never cached. RFC 9111 section 1.2.2 requires treating these as 2^31 seconds.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:99`

## Problem
max-age, s-maxage and stale-while-revalidate are parsed with long.TryParse and passed to TimeSpan.FromSeconds (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:80-86, 93-99, 106-112). TimeSpan.FromSeconds throws OverflowException above ~922,337,203,685 s, so any 12- to 19-digit value throws out of ParseCacheControl; a value of 20+ digits fails long.TryParse and the directive is silently dropped (falling back to Expires, :140-159). RFC 9111 section 1.2.2 requires treating such values as 2^31. Callers: PrepareEntryForStorage (CacheInterceptor.cs:593, background store: the response is not cached and 'Background store failed' is logged), MergeNotModifiedEntry (:722, called in the foreground from CompleteNotModifiedRevalidationAsync, CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:50, after the 304 body was disposed) and the request-header parse in Wrap (:318). Tests cover only the Expires-Date overflow (CacheInterceptorTests.RepresentationDates.cs:95-118).

**Failure scenario.** A stale entry is revalidated and the origin (or a hostile peer) answers 304 with `Cache-Control: max-age=999999999999`. MergeNotModifiedEntry throws OverflowException inside RevalidationHandler.OnResponseStartAsync: the caller gets a handler fault (not a UHttpException and not the stored response) for a revalidation that succeeded, and this repeats on every request until the entry is removed. On a 200 the same header means the response is never cached; `max-age=99999999999999999999, Expires: <past>` is treated as already expired instead of long-lived.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 1.2.2

## Suggested fix
Parse delta-seconds with one helper that accepts only digits, saturates on overflow and clamps to 2^31 seconds (section 1.2.2) before building the TimeSpan; use it for all three directives and for the request side. Add tests for 12-digit and 20-digit values on 200 and 304.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One delta-seconds helper accepts only digits, saturates on overflow and clamps to 2^31 seconds, and is used for max-age, s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate and the request-side parse
- [ ] A 304 with max-age=999999999999 completes the revalidation and serves the stored entry without an exception
- [ ] A 200 with a 12-digit and a 20-digit max-age is cached with the clamped lifetime
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-protocol-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. max-age, s-maxage and stale-while-revalidate go long.TryParse -> TimeSpan.FromSeconds without a bound (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:80-86, 93-99, 106-112); FromSeconds throws OverflowException above ~9.22e11 s, so 12- to 19-digit values throw out of ParseCacheControl, and 20+ digit values fail long.TryParse and the directive is dropped (fallback to Expires, :140-159). RFC 9111 section 1.2.2 requires treating such values as 2^31. No catch on the paths: MergeNotModifiedEntry (:722) runs in the foreground inside CompleteNotModifiedRevalidationAsync (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:50) after the 304 body was disposed, so the exception leaves RevalidationHandler.OnResponseStartAsync and fails the caller; StoreResponseAsync catches only OperationCanceledException (CacheInterceptor.cs:959), so on a 200 the store faults and is logged by QueueBackgroundWork (:1212-1225); the request-side parse at :318 is also unguarded. Tests cover only the Expires-Date overflow (CacheInterceptorTests.RepresentationDates.cs:95-118). Impact is limited to the responses of the origin that sends such a value (unlike cache-protocol-01), hence medium.

Related: [[R11-cache-protocol-01]].

title: [Core] HTTP-date parsing is duplicated in Cache, Retry and Files with different strictness and no shared Core helper
body:
## Summary
Cache uses lenient DateTime.TryParse, Retry uses lenient DateTimeOffset.TryParse for Retry-After, and Files accepts only the 'r' format; Core has no HTTP-date helper. Values such as 'Expires: 2030-01-01' are accepted by Cache although RFC 9111 section 5.3 requires treating them as already expired, and lenient parsing can differ between Mono and IL2CPP.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:180`

## Problem
Cache: DateTime.TryParse with InvariantCulture, lenient (Parsing.cs:180-197), used for Expires and Date. Retry: DateTimeOffset.TryParse, lenient, for Retry-After (Retry/RetryDetectorHandler.cs:140-148). Files: DateTimeOffset.TryParseExact with format 'r' only (Files/FileDownloader.cs:527-535). Core has no HTTP-date helper (rg 'HttpDate' in Runtime/Core finds none). Cache-Control parsing itself is not duplicated outside Cache.

**Failure scenario.** 'Expires: 2030-01-01' or '01/02/2030' is not an HTTP-date and RFC 9111 section 5.3 requires treating it as already expired; Cache's lenient parser accepts it and keeps the entry fresh for years, while FileDownloader would reject the same value. Lenient DateTime.TryParse results can also differ between Mono and IL2CPP class libraries.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 5.6.7; RFC 9111 section 5.3

## Suggested fix
Add one internal HTTP-date parser to Core (IMF-fixdate plus the two obsolete formats of RFC 9110 section 5.6.7) and use it from Cache, Retry and Files.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One internal HTTP-date parser in Core accepts IMF-fixdate and the two obsolete formats of RFC 9110 section 5.6.7 and rejects everything else
- [ ] Cache (Expires, Date), Retry (Retry-After) and Files use that parser
- [ ] An Expires value such as '2030-01-01' is treated as already expired
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Any non-304 answer to a validation request, including a transient 5xx or 429, removes the stored cache entry
body:
## Summary
RevalidationHandler sends every status other than 304 to CompleteModifiedRevalidationAsync, which removes the stored entry before inspecting the status. The same path runs for background stale-while-revalidate refreshes. A short origin outage therefore deletes valid entries and forces full downloads afterwards.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:92`

## Problem
RevalidationHandler routes every status other than 304 to CompleteModifiedRevalidationAsync (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:217-241), which removes the stored entry before looking at the status (:87-98). The same code runs for background stale-while-revalidate revalidation (RunBackgroundRevalidationAsync, CacheInterceptor.cs:489-496). RFC 9111 section 4.3.3 only requires replacing the stored response by a full response and lets a cache forward a 5xx or keep using the stored response.

**Failure scenario.** An entry with an ETag is inside its stale-while-revalidate window. The background revalidation gets 503 during a short outage: the entry is deleted, so the next foreground requests miss and hit the failing origin, and after recovery a full download replaces what would have been a 304.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.3.3; RFC 5861 3

## Suggested fix
Remove the stored entry only when the validation response is a full successful response or a status that implies the representation is gone (404/410); for 5xx/429/408 forward the response and keep the entry.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The stored entry is removed only when the validation response is a full successful response or implies the representation is gone (404, 410)
- [ ] A 5xx, 429 or 408 answer to a validation request is forwarded and the stored entry is kept
- [ ] A failing background revalidation (503) keeps the entry for later requests
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Storage exceptions on foreground lookup, 304 merge and unsafe-method invalidation fail the HTTP request while background stores are best-effort
body:
## Summary
Background cache stores catch and log storage faults, but the foreground paths (Storage.GetAsync, stale-entry removal, 304 merge, post-revalidation removal, unsafe-method invalidation) do not. With a custom ICacheStorage that throws, a POST that the server already processed is reported as failed and may be retried, and a GET the network could answer fails. The exception also surfaces as UHttpErrorType.Unknown.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:143`

## Problem
Background stores catch and log storage faults (CacheInterceptor.cs:968-987) and the comment at 1164-1168 states mutations are best-effort. The foreground paths have no such handling: TryLookupAsync awaits Storage.GetAsync unguarded (CacheInterceptor.cs:545) and the stale-entry removal at 378; the 304 path awaits ReplaceStoredEntryAsync/StorePreparedEntryQueuedAsync and RemoveStoredEntryAsync (StreamingDispatch.cs:61-63, 69); CompleteModifiedRevalidationAsync aborts the fresh response body and rethrows when the removal fails (92-98); UnsafeInvalidationHandler aborts the body and rethrows when invalidation fails (143-152). The exception leaves the dispatch as a non-UHttpException (mapped to Unknown by the bridge). Tests cover only a failing SetAsync in the background store (CacheInterceptorTests.VariantsAndAsync.cs:505-545).

**Failure scenario.** A custom file-backed ICacheStorage throws IOException from RemoveAsync (disk full, file locked). POST /orders is processed by the server and returns 201; invalidation throws, the response body is aborted and the caller sees a failed request, so the app retries the non-idempotent POST. Likewise a GetAsync fault fails a GET that the network could have answered, and a SetAsync fault on a 304 fails a request for which a valid stored body is in hand.

## Suggested fix
Treat storage as best-effort everywhere: a failed lookup is a miss, a failed 304 merge still serves the entry, and a failed removal/invalidation is logged (optionally followed by dropping the index bucket) while the response is delivered untouched.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A failed lookup is treated as a miss and the request goes to the network
- [ ] A failed 304 merge still serves the stored entry; a failed removal or invalidation is logged and the response is delivered unchanged
- [ ] A POST answered 201 whose invalidation throws still returns the 201 response to the caller
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-design-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Foreground storage calls are unguarded: Storage.GetAsync in TryLookupAsync (CacheInterceptor.cs:545), Storage.RemoveAsync for a stale non-revalidatable entry (:378), ReplaceStoredEntryAsync/StorePreparedEntryQueuedAsync/RemoveStoredEntryAsync in the 304 path (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:61-63, :69; the Core methods at CacheInterceptor.cs:1039-1069 have no catch), CompleteModifiedRevalidationAsync aborts the body and rethrows (StreamingDispatch.cs:87-98) and UnsafeInvalidationHandler does the same after a 2xx/3xx to an unsafe method (:141-153). Background stores catch and log (CacheInterceptor.cs:968-987) and :1164-1168 calls mutations best-effort, so the policy is inconsistent. Non-UHttpException faults are wrapped as UHttpErrorType.Unknown (UHttpClient.cs:429-434). The only storage-fault test is the background SetAsync case (Tests/Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptorTests.cs:138-159, VariantsAndAsync.cs:506). MemoryCacheStorage itself throws only when disposed or cancelled, so this is reachable in practice with a custom store (or a shared storage disposed early); the POST case reports failure for a request the server already processed.

title: [Cache] Unsafe-method invalidation is skipped when the caller's token is cancelled after the non-error response has arrived
body:
## Summary
UnsafeInvalidationHandler passes the caller's CancellationToken to the queued invalidation, and the queue skips the mutation when that token is cancelled. If the caller cancels as the headers of a 200 to a POST arrive, the cached GET stays fresh although RFC 9111 section 4.4 requires invalidation once a non-error response is received.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:145`

## Problem
UnsafeInvalidationHandler passes the dispatch CancellationToken to InvalidateAfterUnsafeResponseAsync (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:141-153). InvalidateUriAsync queues the mutation with that token (CacheInterceptor.cs:513-525); RunQueuedMutationAsync skips the mutation and throws when the token is already cancelled (:1190-1195), and MemoryCacheStorage.RemoveAsync waits on its gate with the same token (MemoryCacheStorage.cs:133).

**Failure scenario.** A POST /cart is answered 200; the caller's token is cancelled (scene unload, user abort) just as the headers arrive. The invalidation is skipped, the request ends as cancelled, and the still fresh cached GET /cart is served as a HIT afterwards although the origin applied the change. RFC 9111 section 4.4 requires invalidation once a non-error response to an unsafe method is received.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.4

## Suggested fix
Run the invalidation with the interceptor's background token (not the caller's) and do not let the caller's cancellation skip it once the status is known.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Invalidation after a non-error response to an unsafe method runs with the interceptor's background token, not the caller's
- [ ] Cancelling the caller's token after the response status is known does not skip the invalidation
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] BackgroundRevalidationSink downloads up to 8 MiB of a replacement body that will not be stored
body:
## Summary
The background revalidation sink reads any non-buffered body until EOF or the 8 MiB limit without knowing whether the cache tee is behind it. A no-store 200, a 5xx with a body or an oversized replacement is still downloaded over the user's possibly metered connection before being discarded.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:293`

## Problem
The sink reads any non-buffered body until EOF or _maxBodyBytes (:293-311) without knowing whether a tee is behind it. CompleteModifiedRevalidationAsync routes the response through CacheStoringHandler (:101-103), which passes the transport body through untouched when the status is not storable or Length exceeds the limit (CacheStoringHandler.cs:60-76), and otherwise tees it even when the headers forbid storing (see cache-runtime-01).

**Failure scenario.** Background revalidation of a stale entry receives 200 with Cache-Control: no-store, a 5xx with a body, or a 50 MB replacement (Content-Length above the 8 MiB limit): the sink still reads up to 8 MiB over the user's (possibly metered) connection and then discards it or aborts.

## Suggested fix
Have the sink read only when the body it receives is the cache tee for a storable response; otherwise Abort (or DisposeAsync, for the transport's bounded drain) immediately.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sink reads the body only when it is the cache tee of a storable response; otherwise it aborts or disposes immediately
- [ ] A background revalidation answered with Cache-Control: no-store transfers no more than the already received bytes
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Vary request header values are embedded verbatim in storage keys and CacheEntry.VaryKey, and the sensitive-Vary guard covers only Authorization and Cookie
body:
## Summary
BuildVaryKey puts each nominated request header value into the key passed to ICacheStorage and exposed as CacheEntry.VaryKey. Only authorization and cookie are in the sensitive list, so Vary: X-Api-Key or X-Auth-Token stores the secret in clear text in the key, and a disk-backed storage may write it to a file name or index. Applications using custom storage are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:79`

## Problem
BuildVaryKey appends each nominated request header value as `name=len:value;` (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:54-87, 384-390); the result becomes part of the key passed to ICacheStorage.GetAsync/SetAsync/RemoveAsync and the public CacheEntry.Key/VaryKey (CacheInterceptor.cs:647-662). SensitiveVaryHeaders lists only authorization and cookie (CacheInterceptor.cs:72-76), so `Vary: X-Api-Key`, `X-Auth-Token` or `Proxy-Authorization` responses are stored with the secret inside the key; with AllowVaryAuthorization/AllowVaryCookie the bearer token or cookie string is in the key too.

**Failure scenario.** A project implements ICacheStorage on disk and uses the key as file name or index column. An origin sends `Vary: X-Api-Key`: the API key is written in clear text to the cache directory (and, through the CacheRevalidate event, to the timeline), although X-Api-Key is on RedactionPolicy's default sensitive list.

## Suggested fix
Put a hash (e.g. SHA-256, truncated) of each Vary value into the key instead of the value, and extend the sensitive list to the names in RedactionPolicy.DefaultSensitiveHeaderNames.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Vary header values are replaced by a truncated SHA-256 hash in the storage key and CacheEntry.VaryKey
- [ ] The sensitive-Vary list covers every name in RedactionPolicy.DefaultSensitiveHeaderNames
- [ ] No storage key or CacheRevalidate event contains a raw X-Api-Key, Authorization or Cookie value
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] The cache has no partition key, so one CacheInterceptor serves a response stored for one user or cookie state to the next
body:
## Summary
The base cache key is method plus normalized URI and only Vary adds a secondary key. A response to a cookie-authenticated request with max-age and no Vary is stored and served to the next identity on the same CacheInterceptor, for example after logout and login on one device. This is permitted for a private cache but needs a partition key; it is tracked by #117 step 2.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:105`

## Problem
BuildBaseKey is method + normalized URI (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:105-108); the only secondary key is Vary (:110-113). Responses to requests with a Cookie header are stored by default when the response has no Set-Cookie and no Vary: Cookie (CacheInterceptor.cs:590-618), and `Cache-Control: public` responses to authorized requests are stored without the token in the key (:596-601). Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:31-33 recommends sharing one cache between clients.

**Failure scenario.** User A (session cookie in the CookieJar) fetches GET /api/profile answered with `max-age=300` and no Vary. A logs out, B logs in on the same device within 5 minutes: B's GET /api/profile is a HIT with A's profile.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 2

## Suggested fix
Covered by #117 step 2 (per-user/auth partition key). Until then, expose a partition delegate or a Clear-on-identity-change hook on CacheInterceptor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CacheInterceptor offers a partition key (delegate or identity-change clear hook) that is part of the cache key
- [ ] Entries stored under one partition are not returned for another
- [ ] Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md describes the partitioning and shared-cache guidance
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] The cache key ignores a caller-supplied Host header, so two virtual hosts reached through one URL share entries
body:
## Summary
BuildBaseKey uses only request.Uri, while the HTTP/1.1 serializer sends a caller-set Host header as is. Requests to the same IP URL with different Host headers therefore hit the same cached entry and can receive another virtual host's response.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:107`

## Problem
BuildBaseKey uses only request.Uri (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:105-108; NormalizeUri, CacheInterceptor.UriNormalization.cs:16-42). The HTTP/1.1 serializer sends a caller-set Host header as is and derives one only when it is absent (Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:310-313). RFC 9111 section 2 keys on the target URI, whose authority is what Host carries.

**Failure scenario.** A client talks to a load balancer by IP: GET http://10.0.0.5/config with `Host: a.example` is cached (max-age=300); GET http://10.0.0.5/config with `Host: b.example` is then a HIT with a.example's configuration.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 2; RFC 9110 7.1

## Suggested fix
Include an explicit Host header value (lower-cased) in the base key when it differs from the URI authority, or bypass the cache for such requests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An explicit Host header that differs from the URI authority is included (lower-cased) in the cache key, or the cache is bypassed for such requests
- [ ] GET http://10.0.0.5/config with Host: a.example and with Host: b.example do not share an entry
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] LINQ sort and array allocation on every cache lookup under _indexLock in GetSignatureSnapshot
body:
## Summary
GetSignatureSnapshot runs OrderBy and ToArray inside lock(_indexLock) on every cacheable GET, and TryResolveVary does the same per stored response. This allocates on the cache hit path and lengthens lock hold time, against the allocation rule in CLAUDE.md section 4, and is costly on IL2CPP mobile.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:160`

## Problem
GetSignatureSnapshot runs bucket.Signatures.OrderBy(s => s, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToArray() inside lock(_indexLock) (Variants.cs:152-162) and is called for every cacheable GET (CacheInterceptor.cs:534); the empty signature is registered for non-Vary entries too (Variants.cs:181-186), so the common single-signature hit pays it. TryResolveVary uses OrderBy/ToArray per stored response (Variants.cs:50). CLAUDE.md section 4 bans LINQ on hot paths; Cache is the only shipping feature module importing System.Linq (Core/ProxySettings and Testing are the others).

**Failure scenario.** Each cache hit allocates an ordered-enumerable, a sorter, a buffer and an array while holding the lock that stores and invalidations also need; on IL2CPP mobile this is avoidable GC and lock hold time on the path the cache exists to make cheap.

## Suggested fix
Keep the signatures in a sorted array (or List kept sorted on insert) inside the bucket and return it directly when it has one element; sort with Array.Sort in TryResolveVary.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bucket signatures are kept in a sorted array or list and returned directly when there is one element; TryResolveVary sorts with Array.Sort
- [ ] A cache hit for a non-Vary entry allocates 0 bytes in the signature lookup (measured with an allocation test)
- [ ] Cache no longer imports System.Linq
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] The variant index bounds the number of base keys but not the storage keys per base key, so evicted Vary variants accumulate without limit
body:
## Summary
RegisterStoredVariant adds every stored variant key to the bucket and only the bucket count is bounded. Storage evicts silently, so keys of evicted variants stay in the bucket until the exact same header value is requested again. An origin that varies on a per-request header (trace id, nonce, timestamp) grows memory by one key string per response without limit, and a later invalidation issues one RemoveAsync per leaked key.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:187`

## Problem
RegisterStoredVariant adds every stored variant's key to bucket.StorageKeys and SignatureByStorageKey (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:182-187); the only bound is on `_variantIndex.Count` (:191). MemoryCacheStorage evicts silently (MemoryCacheStorage.cs:102-106, 252-265), and UnregisterStoredVariant runs only for the exact key of the current request on a storage miss (CacheInterceptor.cs:546-550), on explicit removal (:379, :1068) or on invalidation. A variant that was evicted from storage and is never requested again with the same header value stays in the bucket forever. The #60 test varies the URL, not the Vary value (CacheInterceptorTests.Lifecycle.cs:16-46).

**Failure scenario.** An origin answers a polled URL with `Cache-Control: max-age=60` and `Vary: X-Request-Id` (or any header the app sends with a per-request value: a timestamp, nonce, signature, traceparent). Every response is a new variant: storage keeps the newest 100, but the bucket keeps one key string (URL plus header value) per request for the life of the interceptor, and the variants push every other entry out of the 100-entry storage. One request per second leaks tens of MB per day, and a later unsafe-method invalidation issues one RemoveAsync per leaked key (InvalidateBaseKeyCoreAsync, CacheInterceptor.cs:1078-1082).

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.1

## Suggested fix
Bound variants per base key (e.g. a small per-bucket LRU that removes the oldest variant from storage, as QueueEvictedVariantRemoval already does for buckets), and refuse to store when the bound is hit repeatedly. Add a test that sends 10,000 distinct Vary values to one URL and asserts the bucket size.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The number of variants per base key is bounded; the oldest variant is removed from storage and the index when the bound is exceeded
- [ ] Storing is refused when the bound is hit repeatedly
- [ ] A test sending 10,000 distinct Vary values to one URL asserts the bucket size stays at or below the bound
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-protocol-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RegisterStoredVariant adds each stored key to bucket.StorageKeys/SignatureByStorageKey (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:182-187); the only bound is the bucket count (:191). MemoryCacheStorage evicts and sweeps silently (MemoryCacheStorage.cs:102-106, 252-278). TryLookupAsync unregisters only the key built from the current request's header values (CacheInterceptor.cs:542-549), which for a new Vary value was never registered, so keys of evicted/expired variants are removed only by a repeat request with the same value, explicit removal (:379, :1068) or invalidation (TakeStorageKeys). A URL whose response names in Vary a header the client sends with per-request values therefore grows the bucket by one key string per stored response without limit, and a later invalidation issues one RemoveAsync per leaked key (:1078-1082). The #60 test varies the URL, not the Vary value (CacheInterceptorTests.Lifecycle.cs:16-46). Condition: the client must actually send a per-request-varying header (trace id, timestamp, signature); a Vary header on absent or constant request headers always maps to the same key. Contradicts the 'every peer-controlled size is bounded' rule.

Also reported as `cache-runtime-05` (merged into this issue).

title: [Cache] Vary variant index is not persisted or rebuildable from ICacheStorage, so persistent or shared stores lose Vary responses and can serve invalidated variants
body:
## Summary
CacheInterceptor derives storage keys for Vary responses from an in-memory variant index, and ICacheStorage offers no enumeration or metadata record from which the index could be rebuilt. After a restart, or with a second interceptor sharing a custom store, every lookup of a Vary response misses, and invalidation removes only the unvaried key. A persistent custom store therefore gets a 0% hit rate for Vary responses and can serve a pre-invalidation variant as a HIT.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:105`

## Problem
Lookup derives storage keys from the in-memory _variantIndex (CacheInterceptor.cs:105-112, 534-553); with no bucket it tries only the unvaried key 'base|~' (535-536, Variants.cs:110-113). The comment states the index 'is intentionally not persisted across process restarts in v1'. ICacheStorage (ICacheStorage.cs:10-42) has no key enumeration, prefix lookup or metadata record from which the index could be rebuilt, and InvalidateBaseKeyCoreAsync removes only the unvaried key plus keys the index knows (CacheInterceptor.cs:1071-1083). DecompressionInterceptor sits inside the cache in the canonical order, so every 'Vary: Accept-Encoding' response gets a varied key ('base|accept-encoding=~;'). The interface also forces a full-body load per lookup (CacheEntry.Body is ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, ICacheStorage.cs:44-47), even when the lookup ends in revalidation or removal. MemoryCacheStorage is the only shipped implementation, so the abstraction's only purpose is custom (persistent) stores.

**Failure scenario.** A disk-backed ICacheStorage holds 500 CDN responses with 'Vary: Accept-Encoding'. After an app restart (or from a second CacheInterceptor sharing the store) every lookup tries 'base|~' and misses: 0% hit rate for Vary responses at cold/offline start, and the old entries stay orphaned. Worse: a pre-restart variant (Accept-Language: fr) survives a POST invalidation after restart (index empty); a later GET with 'en' re-registers the signature and the next 'fr' GET is served the pre-POST entry as HIT.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 section 4.1, section 4.4

## Suggested fix
Persist the variant signature list through the storage (e.g. a small per-base-key record stored under the unvaried key, as RFC 9111 section 4.1 suggests) and resolve variants from it on lookup and invalidation; split metadata lookup from body retrieval so disk stores need not load bodies for decisions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The variant signature set for a base key is persisted through ICacheStorage (for example as a record under the unvaried key) and is used to resolve variants on lookup and on invalidation
- [ ] After an interceptor restart over the same store, a stored 'Vary: Accept-Encoding' response is a HIT
- [ ] After a restart, a POST to the same URI invalidates all stored variants of that base key, and a later GET never serves a pre-POST variant
- [ ] Metadata lookup is separable from body retrieval so a disk store need not load bodies for freshness or removal decisions
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-design-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: TryLookupAsync builds candidate keys only from GetSignatureSnapshot; with no bucket it tries the unvaried key 'base|~' alone (CacheInterceptor.cs:534-545, Variants.cs:110-113, :152-162). A response with Vary: Accept-Encoding stored while Decompression sits inside the cache gets key 'base|accept-encoding=~;' (BuildVaryKey, Variants.cs:54-87), which a fresh index can never derive. ICacheStorage has no enumeration or prefix lookup (ICacheStorage.cs:10-42), and InvalidateBaseKeyCoreAsync removes only the unvaried key plus index-known keys (CacheInterceptor.cs:1071-1083). The stale-variant trace holds for a persistent store: after a restart POST removes 'base|~' only; a later GET with another Accept-Language re-registers the signature (Variants.cs:185-186) and the next GET with the old value finds the pre-POST entry and serves it as HIT if still fresh. The code itself names this hazard for index eviction (Variants.cs:242-244) and guards it there, but not for an empty index over a non-empty store. The comment at CacheInterceptor.cs:105-107 calls the index an 'accelerator only' and 'intentionally not persisted'; the first part is wrong, since it is the only route to Vary entries. Only custom persistent or shared stores are affected (MemoryCacheStorage is the only shipped one, and dies with the process), hence medium.

Related: #117, [[R11-cache-design-05]].

title: [Cache] Freshness and resident time use DateTime.UtcNow, so moving the device clock back extends freshness without bound
body:
## Summary
The cache computes freshness and resident time from the wall clock (DateTime.UtcNow), including the MemoryCacheStorage sweep. If the device clock is set back, entries stay fresh for the amount of the shift and Age is reported as 0. The storage is in-process, so a monotonic source would be exact.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:122`

## Problem
The cache clock is `DateTime.UtcNow` (CacheInterceptor.cs:122). ExpiresAtUtc is an absolute wall-clock instant computed at response time (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:165-167) and IsFresh compares it with the current wall clock (CacheEntry.cs:135-141); ComputeCurrentAgeSeconds clamps a negative resident time to 0 (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:364-369). MemoryCacheStorage sweeps with DateTime.UtcNow as well (MemoryCacheStorage.cs:87). The storage is in-process, so a monotonic source would be exact.

**Failure scenario.** A response with max-age=60 is cached. The player moves the device clock back one day (a common timer cheat). The entry is now fresh for a day and a minute, with Age reported as 0, so server-driven state that the game re-fetches every minute stops updating.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.2.3

## Suggested fix
Record a monotonic timestamp (Stopwatch) next to CachedAtUtc for in-process entries and derive resident time from it; keep the wall clock only for Date/Expires arithmetic and for entries loaded from persistent storage.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In-process entries record a monotonic timestamp (Stopwatch) next to CachedAtUtc and derive resident time and freshness from it
- [ ] Setting the wall clock back does not extend the freshness of a cached response; Age does not drop to 0 because of it
- [ ] Wall-clock time is used only for Date/Expires arithmetic and for entries loaded from persistent storage
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] CachePolicy is held by reference and read per request, and a default MemoryCacheStorage created by the policy has no owner
body:
## Summary
CacheInterceptor keeps the caller's CachePolicy instance and reads its fields on every request, while the storage ownership flag and variant index capacity are fixed at construction. Reusing a policy across interceptors or assigning policy.Storage later leaves the index describing the old storage, and policy.Storage = null causes NullReferenceException on every request. The default MemoryCacheStorage created by the CachePolicy property initializer is never disposed.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:271`

## Problem
The constructor keeps the caller's CachePolicy instance (CacheInterceptor.cs:273-282) and every decision reads _policy.* live, including _policy.Storage on each call (378, 545, 975, 1044, 1067, 1082), while _ownsStorage and _variantIndexCapacity are fixed at construction (276-292). RetryInterceptor snapshots its policy (Retry/RetryInterceptor.cs:27) and architecture.md's 'Shared config' contract asks for clones. CachePolicy.Storage defaults to 'new MemoryCacheStorage()' in a property initializer (58): with 'new CacheInterceptor(new CachePolicy { ... })' (the documented form, APIReference.md:252) _ownsStorage is false, so Dispose (856-857) never disposes a storage the caller did not create either; setting Storage afterwards discards the default instance undisposed. HeuristicFreshnessLifetime accepts negative values.

**Failure scenario.** Code that reuses one CachePolicy for two interceptors, or assigns policy.Storage after constructing the interceptor (e.g. switching to a per-user store on login): the variant index and capacity still describe the old storage, lookups of Vary entries miss, the index evicts against the wrong bound, and policy.Storage = null turns every request into a NullReferenceException.

## Suggested fix
Snapshot the policy in the constructor (copy constructor as in RetryPolicy, storage captured once), validate it there, and make ownership explicit (e.g. a DisposeStorage flag or owning any storage the policy created itself).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CacheInterceptor snapshots the policy in its constructor (copy as RetryPolicy does) and captures the storage once
- [ ] The constructor validates the policy, including rejecting a null Storage and negative HeuristicFreshnessLifetime, with a clear exception
- [ ] Storage ownership is explicit and a storage created by the policy itself is disposed with the interceptor
- [ ] Mutating the policy after construction does not change interceptor behaviour
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Variant index capacity is taken from the concrete MemoryCacheStorage type, so other ICacheStorage implementations are capped at 4096 base keys and lose Vary entries
body:
## Summary
The constructor sets the variant index capacity by testing whether Storage is MemoryCacheStorage, otherwise using 4096. When the index overflows, the interceptor removes the evicted keys' varied entries from the user's store. A custom store, or a decorator around MemoryCacheStorage, is silently limited to 4096 Vary base keys regardless of its own limits.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:290`

## Problem
The constructor sets _variantIndexCapacity = Storage is MemoryCacheStorage ? memoryStorage.MaxEntries (an internal property) : DefaultVariantIndexCapacity (CacheInterceptor.cs:288-292, Variants.cs:116). The only override, VariantIndexCapacity, is internal ('Test hook', Variants.cs:130-150). When the index exceeds the capacity RegisterStoredVariant evicts the least recent bucket and QueueEvictedVariantRemoval calls Storage.RemoveAsync for its varied keys (Variants.cs:191-196, 245-273). A decorator around MemoryCacheStorage (metrics, logging) also falls to 4096.

**Failure scenario.** A custom disk store sized for 20,000 assets, all served with 'Vary: Accept-Encoding': once 4097 distinct URLs are stored the interceptor starts removing the least recently used URLs' entries from the user's store, silently capping it at 4096 entries regardless of the store's own limits.

## Suggested fix
Expose the bound on the abstraction (a CachePolicy.VariantIndexCapacity setting or an optional capacity-reporting interface) instead of a type test, or remove the need for the bound by resolving variants through the storage (see cache-design-04).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The variant index bound is configurable through the public API (a CachePolicy setting or an optional capacity-reporting interface), not a concrete-type test
- [ ] A decorator around MemoryCacheStorage uses the same bound as the undecorated storage
- [ ] Variant index eviction never removes entries from a custom store that has not asked for it
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-design-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The constructor uses 'Storage is MemoryCacheStorage ? memoryStorage.MaxEntries : DefaultVariantIndexCapacity' (CacheInterceptor.cs:290-292; MaxEntries is internal, MemoryCacheStorage.cs:48; default 4096 at Variants.cs:116), and the only setter is the internal VariantIndexCapacity test hook (Variants.cs:130-150). Beyond the capacity RegisterStoredVariant evicts the least recent bucket and RemoveEvictedVariantsCoreAsync calls Storage.RemoveAsync for its varied keys (Variants.cs:191-196, :222-273). Every stored response registers a bucket, so a custom store ends up with at most 4096 indexed base keys and loses Vary entries beyond that; unvaried entries stay. Low: only custom stores larger than 4096 URLs are affected and the effect is lost hits, not wrong content; it mostly disappears if cache-design-04 is fixed through the storage.

title: [Cache] Request Cache-Control max-age, min-fresh, max-stale and only-if-cached are ignored, so max-age=0 still gets a cache HIT
body:
## Summary
The cache parses the request Cache-Control but acts only on no-cache and no-store. A request with max-age=0 or max-age=5 is answered from an older entry, including a stale-while-revalidate stale one, and only-if-cached goes to the network on a miss. RFC 9111 treats these request directives as optional, so this is a capability gap, but it surprises apps using the max-age=0 reload idiom and prevents offline reads.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:319`

## Problem
Wrap parses the request's Cache-Control (CacheInterceptor.cs:318) but uses only NoCache (:319) for the lookup decision and NoStore at store time (:603). ParseCacheControl does read max-age into MaxAge, yet nothing compares the entry's current age with it; min-fresh, max-stale and only-if-cached are not parsed at all (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:37-113). The fresh branch (:342) and the stale-while-revalidate branch (:352) are therefore taken regardless of those directives. No test under Tests/Runtime/Cache sends a request max-age/min-fresh/only-if-cached.

**Failure scenario.** The app adds `Cache-Control: max-age=0` (the usual reload idiom) or `max-age=5` to a GET to get data no older than that. The cache answers from a 50-minute-old entry (X-Cache: HIT), or from an already stale entry inside its stale-while-revalidate window (X-Cache: STALE), which RFC 9111 section 5.2.1.1 excludes. `only-if-cached` goes to the network on a miss instead of yielding a 504 (section 5.2.1.7), so it cannot be used for offline reads.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 5.2.1.1, 5.2.1.3, 5.2.1.7

## Suggested fix
Compute the entry's current age (ComputeCurrentAgeSeconds exists) and treat the entry as needing validation when age > request max-age or remaining freshness < min-fresh; never take the stale-while-revalidate branch when the request carries max-age/min-fresh. Parse only-if-cached and synthesize a 504 on a miss. Add tests per directive.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A request max-age smaller than the entry's current age, or min-fresh larger than its remaining freshness, causes validation instead of a HIT
- [ ] The stale-while-revalidate branch is not taken when the request carries max-age or min-fresh
- [ ] only-if-cached on a miss returns a synthesized 504 without contacting the network
- [ ] max-stale handling is implemented or explicitly documented as unsupported
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-protocol-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: Wrap uses only requestCacheControl.NoCache (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:318-319) and NoStore at store time (:603); request max-age is parsed but never compared with the entry age, and min-fresh/max-stale/only-if-cached are not parsed (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:37-113). The RFC claim is overstated: RFC 9111 section 5.2.1 states that request directives are advisory and caches MAY implement them, so ignoring max-age/min-fresh/only-if-cached is permitted; a HIT for `max-age=0` is not a protocol violation. What remains is a feature gap that can surprise an app using the `max-age=0` reload idiom (workaround: `no-cache`, which is honoured), and no offline `only-if-cached` mode. Downgraded to low.

Also reported as `cache-design-17` (merged into this issue).

title: [Cache] Stale-while-revalidate starts one background revalidation per stale hit with no per-key de-duplication or bound
body:
## Summary
Every stale-while-revalidate hit serves the entry and starts a new background conditional request, because nothing records an in-flight revalidation for the key. While the first revalidation is in flight the entry stays stale, so each further request launches another request clone, context and queued store. 50 requests for one URL within a 300 ms origin response produce 50 conditional GETs.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:352`

## Problem
Wrap serves the stale entry and unconditionally clones the request and calls StartBackgroundRevalidation (CacheInterceptor.cs:352-363). StartBackgroundRevalidation/RunBackgroundRevalidationAsync (454-511) keep no record of an in-flight revalidation for the base key; the pending-mutation map only sequences storage writes. The entry stays stale until the first revalidation has stored its result, so every hit in that interval launches another conditional request through 'next' (bypassing outer interceptors such as logging and metrics). Tests cover a single stale hit (CacheInterceptorTests.VariantsAndAsync.cs:353).

**Failure scenario.** A list view requests the same avatar or config URL 50 times while it is inside its stale-while-revalidate window and the origin takes 300 ms: 50 concurrent background conditional GETs are sent, each with its own request clone and context, and 50 stores are queued for one key.

## Spec reference
RFC 5861 section 3

## Suggested fix
Track in-flight background revalidations per base key (reuse the pending-mutation dictionary pattern) and skip starting a second one; consider a small global cap on concurrent background revalidations.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At most one background revalidation is in flight per base key; further stale hits during that time are served without starting another
- [ ] A bound on concurrent background revalidations overall is applied or documented
- [ ] The in-flight record is released on success, failure, cancellation and interceptor dispose
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-design-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:352-362: every stale-while-revalidate hit serves the entry, clones the request and calls StartBackgroundRevalidation unconditionally. StartBackgroundRevalidation (454-468) and RunBackgroundRevalidationAsync (470-511) only hop to the thread pool and call RevalidateAsync through 'next'; there is no in-flight set keyed by baseKey/storage key (rg for inflight/dedup/coalesce in Runtime/Cache finds nothing). The only per-key sequencing is _pendingMutations, which TryLookupAsync awaits (527-532) but which is populated only when the store is queued after the validation response arrives, so nothing is pending during the network round trip and IsStaleWhileRevalidate (CacheEntry.cs:154-162) stays true for every hit in that interval. QueueBackgroundWork (1212-1225) is just a fault logger, no cap. Tests cover only a single stale hit (CacheInterceptorTests.VariantsAndAsync.cs:353, RangeAndStreaming.cs:342) and dispose-cancel (548). Mitigation, not a refutation: the requests go through 'next', so an inner ConcurrencyInterceptor (role order Cache outside Concurrency, InterceptorOrdering.cs:10-18) or the connection pool bounds simultaneous sockets, but the N conditional GETs, N clones/contexts and N queued stores are still issued. RFC 5861 does not mandate de-duplication, so this is a resource/design defect, not a protocol violation; medium is right. No open issue tracks it.

Also reported as `cache-protocol-20`, `cache-runtime-03` (merged into this issue).

title: [Cache] Stale-while-revalidate clones the request after serving the response, racing the caller's request dispose
body:
## Summary
The stale-while-revalidate branch calls request.Clone() only after the cached response has been delivered. For streaming sends the caller may dispose the request in the meantime, so Clone() throws ObjectDisposedException, the fault is ignored, and no background revalidation starts. Nothing is logged.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:360`

## Problem
The branch awaits ServeCachedEntryAsync and only then calls request.Clone() (:358-361). For a streaming send the response task is completed inside OnResponseStartAsync (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/StreamingDispatchBridge.cs:158) and UHttpRequest.SendStreamingAsync disposes the request in its finally (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:397-404); Clone() throws ObjectDisposedException once _disposeRequested is set (:161, :564-574). The exception faults the dispatch task, which the bridge ignores because the response was already delivered (StreamingDispatchBridge.cs:60-61).

**Failure scenario.** A streaming request is served STALE; the caller's continuation runs on another pool thread and disposes the request before the interceptor thread reaches Clone() (more likely when an outer handler completes OnResponseStartAsync asynchronously). No background revalidation starts and nothing is logged.

## Suggested fix
Clone the request before ServeCachedEntryAsync and dispose the clone if serving throws.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The request is cloned before the cached response is served, and the clone is disposed if serving throws
- [ ] A caller disposing the request immediately after the response start does not prevent the background revalidation
- [ ] No clone leaks on any path (success, exception, cancellation, dispose)
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Entry removals and 304 merges act on the entry read at lookup without re-checking it, and one removal bypasses the per-key mutation queue
body:
## Summary
The stale non-revalidatable branch calls Storage.RemoveAsync directly instead of using the per-key mutation queue, and the 304 merge and the 200 removal use the entry read at lookup time. If another request stored a newer entry in between, the older request can delete it or overwrite it with the older body marked fresh for a full lifetime.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:378`

## Problem
The stale, non-revalidatable branch calls _policy.Storage.RemoveAsync(lookup.StorageKey) directly (:378-379), outside the per-key queue every other write uses. The 304 path stores a merge built from the entry read at lookup (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:50-63, body: existing.Body at CacheInterceptor.cs:752) and the 200 path queues an unconditional removal (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:92). None of them re-reads the stored entry inside the queued mutation.

**Failure scenario.** Requests A and B for one key overlap. A looked up stale entry E1 and is slow; B fetched and stored fresh E2. A's direct RemoveAsync (or its queued removal after a 200 whose body the consumer then abandons) deletes E2, costing a refetch; or A's late 304 for E1 overwrites E2 with E1's body marked fresh for a full lifetime.

## Suggested fix
Route the removal through the queue and make remove/merge conditional on the stored entry still being the one that was looked up (compare CachedAtUtc/ETag inside the mutation).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All removals go through the per-key mutation queue
- [ ] Removal and 304 merge are conditional on the stored entry still being the one that was looked up (compare CachedAtUtc or ETag inside the mutation)
- [ ] A late 304 for an older entry never overwrites a newer stored entry
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Timeline events CacheHit, CacheMiss, CacheRevalidate and CacheInvalidated carry the full cache key (query values, Vary header values) and the Monitor does not redact them
body:
## Summary
Cache timeline events record the base key (method plus normalized URI including the query) and, for CacheRevalidate, the storage key with raw Vary request header values. MonitorInterceptor redacts the URL and headers, but copies timeline event data verbatim, and the Editor JSON export writes it. Query secrets such as access_token and Vary header values such as X-Api-Key therefore reach the Monitor and exports in default configuration.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:425`

## Problem
CacheHit/CacheMiss record `key = baseKey` = method + NormalizeUri(uri) including the query (CacheInterceptor.cs:344-347, 354-357, 383-386); CacheRevalidate records `lookup.StorageKey` (:423-426), which appends BuildVaryKey's raw request header values (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:54-87, e.g. `x-api-key=32:<value>;`, or Authorization/Cookie when AllowVary* is on); CacheInvalidated records the normalized URI (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:22-26). MonitorInterceptor redacts the URL and headers with RedactionPolicy (Runtime/Observability/MonitorInterceptor.cs:347-376) but CopyTimelineData stringifies event data verbatim (:661-693), and the Editor export writes it out (Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:164-192). #117 plans one RedactionPolicy for 'exceptions/timeline' but does not name these events or the Vary values.

**Failure scenario.** GET https://api.example/v1/items?access_token=SECRET with default settings: the Monitor shows the URL as redacted, while the same capture's Timeline tab and JSON export contain `key = GET https://api.example/v1/items?access_token=SECRET`. If the origin sends `Vary: X-Api-Key`, the CacheRevalidate event contains the API key value although X-Api-Key is on the default redaction list.

## Suggested fix
Do not put raw keys into event data: record a redacted URL (query values removed) and a short hash of the Vary key, or record nothing but the event name. Independently, apply RedactionPolicy to timeline data in MonitorInterceptor (#117).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Cache timeline events do not contain raw query values or raw Vary header values; they carry a redacted URL and a short hash of the Vary key, or only the event name
- [ ] MonitorInterceptor applies RedactionPolicy to timeline event data
- [ ] The Monitor Timeline tab and the Editor JSON export for a request with ?access_token=SECRET and Vary: X-Api-Key contain neither value
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. CacheHit/CacheMiss record baseKey = method + NormalizeUri(uri), which keeps the query (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:344-347, 354-357, 383-386; CacheInterceptor.UriNormalization.cs:29-41); CacheRevalidate records lookup.StorageKey (:423-426), which embeds raw Vary request header values (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:54-87, 384-390); CacheInvalidated records the normalized URI (CacheInterceptor.StreamingDispatch.cs:22-26). MonitorInterceptor redacts URL and headers (Runtime/Observability/MonitorInterceptor.cs:347-376; default policy redacts query values, RedactionPolicy.cs:49) but CopyTimelineData stringifies event data verbatim (:661-693) and the Editor export writes it (Editor/Monitor/HttpMonitorWindow.Export.cs:164-192). #117 step 1 names 'exceptions/timeline' as RedactionPolicy consumers, so the gap is tracked in general; the issue does not name the cache events or the Vary values in the storage key, which should be added to it.

title: [Cache] When several stored variants match, lookup returns the first by signature order instead of the most recent response
body:
## Summary
TryLookupAsync iterates variant signatures in ordinal order and returns the first entry found, so an older unvaried entry always wins over a newer varied one. After an origin starts sending Vary: Accept-Language, a German request is served the older English entry until it expires. RFC 9111 section 4.1 requires the most recent matching response.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:538`

## Problem
TryLookupAsync iterates the signatures returned by GetSignatureSnapshot, which sorts them ordinally (CacheInterceptor.Variants.cs:160), and returns the first entry found (CacheInterceptor.cs:538-553). The empty signature (no Vary) sorts first, so an older unvaried entry always wins over a newer varied one. RFC 9111 section 4.1 asks for the most recent matching response (by Date).

**Failure scenario.** An origin starts sending `Vary: Accept-Language`. The earlier unvaried English entry is still fresh. A forced reload with `Accept-Language: de` stores the German variant, but every later German request without no-cache is a HIT with the older English entry until it expires.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.1

## Suggested fix
Collect all matching entries and choose the one with the latest Date/CachedAtUtc; when a response with a different Vary set is stored, remove the entries of other signatures for that base key.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When several stored entries match the request, the one with the latest Date/CachedAtUtc is selected
- [ ] Storing a response with a different Vary set removes the entries of other signatures for that base key
- [ ] A German request after a forced reload is served the German variant, not the older unvaried entry

title: [Cache] Dead code and unused parameters in the Cache module
body:
## Summary
The Cache module has an unused PrepareEntryForStorage overload with its SnapshotBodyForCache helper, a QueueMutationAndWaitAsync alias, unread members (CacheLookupResult.Signature, IStreamingCacheAccumulator.Length), an isSharedCache flag that is always false, and an empty CacheStorageCompatibilityNotes class. The flag suggests shared-cache support that does not exist and the dead overload uses different ResponseUrl semantics than the live path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:558`

## Problem
PrepareEntryForStorage(UHttpRequest, UHttpResponse, string) (CacheInterceptor.cs:558-571) has no caller, and SnapshotBodyForCache (833-839) is called only from it. QueueMutationAndWaitAsync (1085-1092) is a pure alias of QueueMutationAsync whose name promises waiting. CacheLookupResult.Signature (214) is never read. ResolveExpiry's isSharedCache flag is false at both call sites (625, 723), so CacheControlDirectives.SharedMaxAge and the s-maxage parser branch (Parsing.cs:77-88, 135-138) are unreachable. IStreamingCacheAccumulator.Length (StreamingCacheAccumulator.cs:8, 17) is never read. CacheStoringHandler takes a RequestContext only to null-check it (CacheStoringHandler.cs:31, 44). CacheStorageCompatibilityNotes is an empty compiled class that only carries a comment (ICacheStorage.cs:44-50). The inner '!expiresAtUtc.HasValue' tests at 643 and 739 are always true.

**Failure scenario.** Maintenance cost: the dead buffered-response overload passes response.Request?.Uri as the response URL while the live path passes requestUri, so a future caller picking the wrong overload changes stored ResponseUrl semantics; the flag argument suggests shared-cache support that does not exist.

## Suggested fix
Delete the unused overload, helper, alias, field, interface member, parameter and placeholder class; drop isSharedCache or wire it to a real policy option.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The unused overload, helper, alias, unread members, null-checked-only RequestContext parameter and placeholder class are removed
- [ ] isSharedCache and the unreachable s-maxage parser branch are removed or wired to a real policy option
- [ ] Always-true '!expiresAtUtc.HasValue' checks are removed
- [ ] Existing Cache tests still pass and no public API is removed without a mention in the PR
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] Hop-by-hop stripping runs before storability checks, so Cache-Control, Vary or Set-Cookie named in Connection is dropped before it is evaluated
body:
## Summary
PrepareEntryForStorage strips headers named by Connection tokens before checking Set-Cookie, parsing Cache-Control and resolving Vary. A response with 'Connection: close, Cache-Control' and 'Cache-Control: no-store' is stored and served because no-store is removed first; 'Connection: Vary' stores a varied response as unvaried. The 304 merge path has the same order.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:588`

## Problem
PrepareEntryForStorage clones the response headers and calls StripHopByHopHeaders first (CacheInterceptor.cs:587-588), which removes every header named by a Connection token (CacheInterceptor.Parsing.cs:290-314). The Set-Cookie check (:590), ParseCacheControl (:593) and TryResolveVary (:609) then read the stripped copy. MergeNotModifiedEntry strips at :705 before :707 and :722.

**Failure scenario.** An HTTP/1.1 response from a misbehaving server or proxy carries `Connection: close, Cache-Control`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Expires` one hour ahead. The no-store directive, addressed to this hop, is dropped before parsing and the response is stored and served for an hour. `Connection: Vary` stores a varied response as unvaried.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 7.6.1; RFC 9111 3.1

## Suggested fix
Evaluate Set-Cookie, Cache-Control and Vary on the headers as received and strip hop-by-hop fields only from the copy that is stored (or refuse to store when Connection nominates a field the cache depends on).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Set-Cookie, Cache-Control and Vary are evaluated on the headers as received
- [ ] Hop-by-hop fields are stripped only from the copy that is stored, in both the store and 304 merge paths
- [ ] A response with 'Connection: Cache-Control' and 'Cache-Control: no-store' is not stored
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Cache] must-revalidate is treated like no-cache, so a response with max-age=N, must-revalidate is revalidated or refetched on every request
body:
## Summary
PrepareEntryForStorage folds no-cache, must-revalidate and Pragma: no-cache into one flag, and CacheEntry.IsFresh returns false whenever it is set. A response with 'max-age=3600, must-revalidate' is therefore never served fresh: with a validator every request is a conditional round trip, without one the entry is removed and refetched. RFC 9111 section 5.2.2.2 only forbids reuse once the response is stale.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:629`

## Problem
PrepareEntryForStorage folds three directives into one flag: `mustRevalidate = responseCacheControl.NoCache || responseCacheControl.MustRevalidate || pragmaNoCache` (CacheInterceptor.cs:629; same at :726 for the 304 merge). CacheEntry.IsFresh is `!MustRevalidate && !IsExpired(utcNow)` (CacheEntry.cs:119-122), so the lookup at CacheInterceptor.cs:342 never takes the HIT branch for such an entry: with a validator it sends a conditional request every time (:365-375); without one it removes the entry and refetches (:378-379), so the store was wasted. RFC 9111 section 5.2.2.2 only forbids reuse of the response once it is stale; while fresh it is reusable without validation. The only must-revalidate tests use max-age=0 (CacheInterceptorTests.Representation.cs:154, DecodedRevalidation.cs:42).

**Failure scenario.** Origin sends `Cache-Control: max-age=3600, must-revalidate` (a very common combination) with an ETag. Expected: one network request per hour. Actual: every request performs a conditional round trip; without ETag/Last-Modified every request is a full download and a store that is thrown away on the next lookup. The cache is ineffective for these responses.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 5.2.2.2, 5.2.2.4, 4.2.4

## Suggested fix
Keep two flags on the entry: 'always validate' (no-cache, Pragma) and 'no stale reuse' (must-revalidate). IsFresh should consult only the first; IsStaleWhileRevalidate and any future stale serving consult both. CacheEntry's public constructor needs the extra field (public API change).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CacheEntry keeps separate state for 'always validate' (no-cache, Pragma) and 'no stale reuse' (must-revalidate); IsFresh consults only the first
- [ ] A response with 'max-age=3600, must-revalidate' is a HIT while fresh and is revalidated or not served once stale
- [ ] Stale-while-revalidate and any stale serving consult both flags
- [ ] The public CacheEntry constructor change is documented with XML docs and mentioned in the PR
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ that fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-protocol-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: mustRevalidate = NoCache || MustRevalidate || pragmaNoCache (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:629, :726) and IsFresh = !MustRevalidate && !IsExpired (CacheEntry.cs:119-122), so `max-age=3600, must-revalidate` never takes the HIT branch at :342; with a validator every request is a conditional round trip (:365-375), without one the entry is removed and refetched (:378-379) after the body was copied for the store. No comment, phase doc or issue documents this as a deliberate trade-off (rg must-revalidate over Development~/docs/phases and Documentation~ finds nothing); tests only use max-age=0 with must-revalidate. Correction to the finding: this is not an RFC violation (a cache may always validate); it is an effectiveness defect that makes the cache useless for a common header combination. No stale or wrong data is served.

title: [Cache] CacheInterceptor serves entries with no freshness information as fresh forever when DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness=false
body:
## Summary
With DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness=false and EnableHeuristicFreshness off, PrepareEntryForStorage stores a response that has no explicit or heuristic freshness with ExpiresAtUtc=null. CacheEntry.IsExpired returns false for a null expiry, so the entry is a HIT for the life of the process and is never revalidated even when it has an ETag. RFC 9111 treats such a response as stale. Apps that opt in to caching validator-only responses are affected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:631`

## Problem
PrepareEntryForStorage (CacheInterceptor.cs:631-645): when ResolveExpiry returns null and the response is not no-cache/must-revalidate, the entry is only rejected if DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness is true; otherwise it is stored with expiresAtUtc null unless EnableHeuristicFreshness is also set. CacheEntry.IsExpired returns false for a null ExpiresAtUtc (CacheEntry.cs:137-138), so IsFresh (:119-122) is always true and the lookup at CacheInterceptor.cs:342 serves a HIT without ever revalidating, even when the entry has an ETag. ShouldEvict (CacheEntry.cs:166-167) never sweeps it either. MergeNotModifiedEntry repeats the logic at :728-741. Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:153 states 'There is no default TTL: an entry lives exactly as long as the response's own freshness allows'. The only test with the flag off also enables heuristics (CacheInterceptorTests.RepresentationDates.cs:128-131).

**Failure scenario.** An app sets `new CachePolicy { DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness = false }` to also keep validator-only responses. GET /api/config answers 200 with an ETag and no Cache-Control/Expires. Every later GET of that URL for the life of the process is answered from memory (X-Cache: HIT) and the origin is never contacted again; a default-cacheable 404/410 without freshness is pinned the same way. RFC 9111 section 4.2 treats a response with neither explicit nor heuristic freshness as stale: it must be validated before reuse.

## Spec reference
RFC 9111 4.2, 4.2.2

## Suggested fix
Treat a missing freshness lifetime as lifetime 0 (stale immediately): store such an entry only when it has a validator and revalidate it on each use, or drop it. Reserve ExpiresAtUtc == null for nothing, or give it an explicit 'always validate' meaning in IsFresh. Add a test with the flag off and heuristics off.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A stored response without explicit or heuristic freshness has a freshness lifetime of 0 and is revalidated (conditional request) on every use, or is not stored; it is never served as a HIT without validation
- [ ] CacheEntry.ExpiresAtUtc == null no longer means 'fresh forever' on either the store path or the 304 merge path (MergeNotModifiedEntry)
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Cache/ fails before the fix and passes after it, covering DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness=false with heuristics off and an ETag-only response

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `cache-protocol-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/cache.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. PrepareEntryForStorage (Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptor.cs:631-645): with ResolveExpiry == null the entry is rejected only when DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness is true (:638); heuristic expiry is assigned only when EnableHeuristicFreshness is also set (:643), otherwise the entry is built with expiresAtUtc null (:657). CacheEntry.IsExpired returns false for null (CacheEntry.cs:137-138), so IsFresh (:119-122) is always true and the lookup serves HIT at CacheInterceptor.cs:342; ShouldEvict returns false (CacheEntry.cs:166-167). MergeNotModifiedEntry repeats it (:728-741). Note heuristics are reachable only with DoNotCacheWithoutFreshness=false, so flipping that flag alone gives never-expiring entries, contradicting Documentation~/Modules/Interceptors.md:153. Non-default opt-in configuration; the only test with the flag off also enables heuristics (Tests/Runtime/Cache/CacheInterceptorTests.RepresentationDates.cs:128-131). Lifetime is bounded only by LRU eviction/process life (or not at all with a persistent ICacheStorage).
